name: Patient Follow-up Visit

anchors.90-100: Clear, accurate and natural clinical English throughout
anchors.70-80: Occasional minor errors without loss of meaning
anchors.50-60: Repeated errors sometimes require listener effort
anchors.30-40: Frequent errors interfere with the consultation
anchors.10-20: Communication is often difficult to understand

anchors.90-100: Accurately reviews the prior plan, response, adherence, adverse effects, results and safety-netting
anchors.70-80: Safe and mostly accurate with only minor omissions
anchors.50-60: Covers the main issue but misses a relevant safety or monitoring point
anchors.30-40: Several important omissions or misleading explanations
anchors.10-20: Unsafe or substantially inaccurate follow-up communication

anchors.90-100: Connects interval change to the prior plan and reaches a clear, evidence-based next step
anchors.70-80: Structured review and reasonable next plan with minor gaps
anchors.50-60: Some longitudinal reasoning but the link between response and plan is incomplete
anchors.30-40: Visit is unfocused or does not meaningfully reassess the prior plan
anchors.10-20: No coherent follow-up reasoning is demonstrated

anchors.90-100: Smooth signposting and efficient transitions across the follow-up agenda
Nonjudgmental adherence discussion, clear explanation, shared decisions and teach-back
anchors.70-80: Respectful and patient-centred with minor missed opportunities
anchors.50-60: Professional but mechanical or insufficiently collaborative
anchors.30-40: Judgmental, dismissive or unclear in important moments
anchors.10-20: Communication undermines trust or patient safety

checklist.item: Confirms the reason for follow-up and the patient's agenda
Links the visit to the previous assessment and plan
Assesses interval improvement, persistence or deterioration
Checks treatment tolerance and adverse effects
Screens for case-relevant new symptoms and red flags
Explains available results or monitoring data in plain English
Elicits concerns, questions and treatment preferences
Agrees on a concrete next plan
Provides follow-up timing and safety-net advice
Uses teach-back or another understanding check

empathy_markers: uses neutral language when discussing adherence
acknowledges the burden or uncertainty of ongoing treatment
invites the patient's questions and preferences
checks understanding of the updated plan
